ledger.claim: The platform's own trip record and the driver-device GPS trace establish the deviation the rider reports. The vehicle left the recommended route at Yishun Avenue 1 / Yio Chu Kang Road at 13:28:02, ran via Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu, and rejoined the recommended line at Sengkang West Avenue / Jalan Kayu at 13:35:58; the recommended line the platform itself recorded was Yishun Avenue 2 - Yishun Avenue 1 - Seletar Road - Sengkang West Avenue. On the platform's recorded distances under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 8.3 km minus 7.3 km = 1.00 km. The rider's account is not contradicted by anything on the record; it is corroborated by the platform's own telemetry, and the driver's answer ('Distance about the same') does not meet it. Both artifacts are COMPLETE with weight 1.0, so the deviation is established, not inferred.

There is no traffic justification for the reroute. The only traffic data on file is the LTA speed-band advisory for Seletar Road - the recommended segment - both directions, covering 12:51:15 to 14:21:15 on the trip date, i.e. the trip window. It records type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure, and speed bands 5-6 throughout. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and NONE is not one of the types the clause admits (its derived justification_kind and justifies_reroute both return false/absent). The driver's stated reason, that 'Jalan Kayu road is smoother', is therefore not a justification the policy recognises: it is a preference for one road over another, pleaded with no supporting data.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, which is what POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log is complete and contiguous with zero messages and no first or last message timestamp, and the trip record carries no in-app calls and no trip call recording; there is thus neither a chat notice nor a recorded verbal notice. Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established, and there is no acknowledgment by the rider anywhere in the record. The reroute was unannounced and unagreed, so the rider cannot be taken to have accepted the longer road.

The deviation returned by the platform is exactly 1.00 km, and POL-RD-22 computes it by subtracting two distances the platform records to one decimal place (8.3 km minus 7.3 km). The tolerance is '1.0 km or less', so the figure sits on the outermost edge of the band, and on distances rounded to 0.1 km the record cannot exclude a true deviation above 1.0 km. The fact the tolerance test needs is therefore not established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 directs that the case go to a human reviewer with the open question stated, rather than be decided against the rider on a figure that lies exactly on the line. The rider's own account - that the route was at least 1 km longer - is consistent with the top of that band, not with a route that was comfortably within it.

The rider's loss is real and measurable, and the remedy the policy provides must be read party-relatively. The fare ledger shows 8.3 km charged at 0.72 SGD/km, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is presently carrying the disputed 1.00 km of distance - 0.72 SGD. If the deviation is found to be above tolerance, POL-RD-24 refunds the excess distance fare in full: 1.00 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.72 SGD, without surge, and that is the sum the rider presses for under POL-RD-24(b)/(d). If the tolerance question is left open on the record, POL-RD-24 also licenses ESCALATE, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case holds the amount rather than collecting it, so the rider would not carry it either. What the rider should not be left with is NO_ACTION, which on this record leaves the rider paying the whole 12.65 SGD, including the distance the driver travelled without telling the rider and with no traffic justification at all.

The platform's own recorded distances put this deviation at exactly the tolerance line: 8.3 km actual less 7.3 km recommended is 1.00 km, and POL-RD-22 provides that a deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. The trip record's derived deviation block returns deviation_km 1.00 with within_tolerance true, so nothing is refundable on this trip.

The traffic record does not justify this reroute, and that is the driver's friend here: the LTA advisory for the recommended Seletar Road segment is type NONE — no incident, roadwork or closure, speed bands 5-6 throughout — so under POL-RD-23 the reroute is not traffic-justified. The row of POL-RD-24 that then applies is row (e), 'not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less', which expressly yields no refund and leaves the present state standing.

The outcome is the same whichever way the traffic question falls, which is what makes this case safe to rule: under POL-RD-24(c) a traffic-justified reroute where the rider was not informed and the deviation is 1 km or less also produces no refund, and under POL-RD-24(e) an unjustified reroute at 1 km or less produces no refund. Both tolerance rows pay nothing, so no reading of the justification can turn a 1.00 km deviation into a refund.

The rider cannot use the GPS trace to stretch the distance in his favour. The trace itself measures only 6.996 km over 34 fixes, and POL-RD-22 is explicit that the trace shows which route was taken and when but is not used to re-measure distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The deviation therefore stands at the platform's recorded 1.00 km, not at any figure the trace might suggest.

Even on the rider's own case the sum is far smaller than he asks for. The only money POL-RD-24 ever moves on a deviation is the excess distance fare — deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — which on a 1.00 km deviation at 0.72 SGD/km is 0.72 SGD, not the 2.50 SGD claimed. The claimed figure has no basis in the matrix.

NO_ACTION is party-relative, and on this record it runs for the driver. The rider is the filing party, and the payments ledger shows the 12.65 SGD metered fare as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, so the fare stays where it is rather than being returned.

The chat log is empty — 0 messages, contiguous, matching the trip record — and the trip record carries no in-app calls, so the driver cannot establish that he notified the rider of the reroute as POL-RD-21 requires, and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. That omission does not open a refund on these facts: POL-RD-24's two tolerance rows, (c) for an uninformed rider and (e) for an unjustified reroute, pay nothing where the deviation is 1 km or less, and no row of the matrix conditions a refund on notification below that line.

No escalation is forced on the routing question. The contested amount is 2.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band in which an AI ruling is final, and neither profile snapshot carries a fraud_flags entry of 1 or more, so no 0.95 threshold is engaged; under POL-RD-25 the ruling stands at 0.80 or more confidence, and the 2 km limb that clause describes is not in force on this record (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, and the trip record's derived block marks over_ai_limit false).

Nothing on this record is impaired: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger, both profile snapshots and the LTA advisory are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired. There is therefore no gap in the evidence that could carry POL-GEN-26's escalation, and the deviation distance, the route taken and the justification are each established on the artifacts above.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is decided on the platform's own recorded distances, and it comes down to a single number: the recommended route was 7.3 km (Yishun Avenue 2 – Yishun Avenue 1 – Seletar Road – Sengkang West Avenue) and the driver travelled 8.3 km (via Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu, rejoining at Sengkang West Avenue). The difference is exactly 1.00 km. POL-RD-22 (Measuring the deviation, v2.1 1.4) sets the distance as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km — that is, 8.3 – 7.3 = 1.00 km — and provides that a deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. 1.00 km is therefore within tolerance, at the line but inside it.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data on file is the LTA advisory for the recommended Seletar Road segment, both directions, covering 12:51–14:21 on the trip date (the trip window). It records type NONE — no congestion, no incident, no closure — and POL-RD-23 (Traffic justification) justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure. NONE is not one of the types that clause admits. The driver's stated reason, that Jalan Kayu is smoother, is a road preference, not a traffic justification the policy recognises.

That places the case squarely in row (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix (v2.1 1.3): not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less — no refund, within tolerance. Row (c) reaches the same result on the traffic-justified branch, so the outcome does not turn on the justification question. No refund is payable, and the present state stands.

On the claims: I accept the driver's points that the deviation is 1.00 km and within tolerance, that the GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance (the 34-fix trace measures 6.996 km and, under POL-RD-22, would understate the route's length), that the reroute was not traffic-justified, that neither tolerance row pays anything, and that no escalation is forced (the contested amount is 2.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band in which an AI ruling is final; neither profile carries fraud_flags of 1 or more; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not in force because ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false and the trip record marks over_ai_limit false). I accept the rider's points that the deviation of 1.00 km is established on the platform's telemetry, that the reroute had no traffic justification, and that the driver did not notify the rider: the chat log is complete and contiguous with zero messages, the trip record carries no in-app calls, and POL-RD-21 treats a verbal notice with no recording as not established. That omission does not change the outcome, because no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix conditions a refund on notification where the deviation is 1 km or less.

I reject the rider's argument that the case should go to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26 because the deviation sits exactly on the tolerance line and distances are recorded to one decimal place. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired. Here nothing is missing or impaired: every artifact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, the two recorded distances the clause's own test reads are both present, and that test defines 'within tolerance' as 1.0 km or less. A test that runs on complete evidence and returns a result decides the limb; the possibility that rounding conceals a slightly larger true figure is speculation, not an impaired reading. The rider's fallback that the excess distance fare of 0.72 SGD (1.00 km × 0.72 SGD/km) is refundable only arises if the deviation is over 1 km, which it is not.

The disputed amount of 2.50 SGD is not collected and not refunded; the metered fare of 12.65 SGD stands as charged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
